column1: # ACTION JK, p171 - the inner grant bodies P170-A COUNTED, now CLASSIFIED by family and
# Sakai  HEAD 88f8e09c0a38 (2026-10-13T09:46:58Z) -- p170 read 10a1d904d379. The tree MOVED, and the
#        server would not serve the pinned sha (`fatal: couldn't find remote ref`), so this limb is
#        an UNCONTROLLED re-read: any difference is tree OR instrument and cannot be separated.
#        The name-match count is 165 at both HEADs and the body count 129 at both, so nothing
#        observed here actually moved -- but that is a result, not a control.
# Moodle HEAD f20534726a59 (2026-10-03) -- IDENTICAL to p170's recorded HEAD. CONTROLLED re-read.
# P170-A's denominator counts any name-matched file whose body contains a licence phrase. P171-A
# adds the step after it: a grant body must BE a licence document, not a SOURCE FILE that mentions
# one. That distinction is worth 105 of Moodle's 193 and 0 of Sakai's 129.
# FAMILY TALLY by distinct DOCUMENT blob (72 blobs)
#   All 3 sit in licenses/ -- a THIRD-PARTY NOTICE MANIFEST, not Sakai's own grant:
#     LGPL-2.1 verbatim  x2 blobs / 5 paths  (LGPL2.1, aopalliance, dnsjava-1.2.3, hibernate-2.1, jboss-j2ee)
#     IBM Public License 1.0  x1 blob / 1 path  (junit-3.8.1.license.txt)
#   NOTE a separate defect, not this action's question: the FILENAME names a component whose real
#   upstream licence differs from the body. aopalliance is public domain upstream and dnsjava is
#   BSD, yet both files carry the LGPL-2.1 text; junit 3.8.1 shipped under CPL-1.0, and this file
#   is its IPL-1.0 predecessor. The manifest is not a reliable per-component map.
# FAMILY TALLY by distinct DOCUMENT blob (80 blobs)
# FALSIFIER: "refuted if any family appears that is INCOMPATIBLE with the repo's outer grant -- a
#   non-elected copyleft inside Sakai's ECL-2.0, or a proprietary/non-commercial body inside either."
# LIMB 2, proprietary / non-commercial: FIRED ON THE RAW MEASUREMENT, SILENT AFTER RESOLUTION.
#   6 raw hostile hits in Moodle, 0 real, in two classes:
#     4 of 6 were GPL-3.0's OWN section 6(b) -- "allowed only occasionally and noncommercially" --
#       a condition on one alternative conveying METHOD inside the GPL. Moodle's own COPYING.txt
#       was one of them. Every full GPL-3.0 body on earth trips a naive search.
#     2 of 6 were Moodle PHP SOURCE FILES: lang/en/license.php and lib/tests/licenselib_test.php,
#       which carry "Creative Commons - NonCommercial" as DATA -- the licence menu Moodle offers
#       its users for uploaded content. Not a grant over Moodle at all.
#   0 bodies in either repository withhold commercial use or redistribution.
# LIMB 1, non-elected copyleft inside Sakai's ECL-2.0: FIRES ON THE LETTER, and p171 does NOT
#   claim it silent. 3 of Sakai's 72 blobs are reciprocal (2 LGPL-2.1, 1 IPL-1.0) and none offers a
#   permissive election. What p171 CAN state as measurement: all 3 are notice files in licenses/,
#   describing third-party components, and 0 copyleft grant governs Sakai's own code. Whether a
#   dependency notice is "copyleft inside the repo" is a READING, and it is counsel's, not an
#   instrument's. Recorded as FIRED-ON-THE-LETTER / RESOLVED-ON-THE-FACTS rather than smoothed.
# SO: gap 115's substantive anxiety is DISCHARGED -- the inner audit is procedural, as penecho's 32
#   predicted. The procedural cost is NOT small and is now sized: 129 + 88 = 217 document bodies
#   across 12 families, and a client scanner will read 105 Moodle source files as licences too.
# T223 - P170-A OVER-READS BY COUNTING SOURCE CODE AS GRANTS, and asymmetrically.
#   Moodle headers EVERY php file with a GPL notice, and ships an admin/tool/licensemanager/
#   subsystem whose filenames all contain "license". The two conventions multiply: 105 of 193
#   "grant bodies" (54%) are source code. Sakai's contamination is 0 of 129, because its grants
#   live in licenses/*.txt. So p170's published pair -- "Sakai 129, Moodle 193" -- invited a
#   comparison that cannot be made: 129 is 129 documents, 193 is 88 documents plus 105 php files.
#   The corrected pair is Sakai 129, Moodle 88 -- and Moodle, the larger tree, carries FEWER.
# T224 - EVERY DEFEAT OF THIS INSTRUMENT THIS PASS WAS FORMATTING, NOT LAW. Four, all caught by
#   its own regression tests before publication: (1) a family name matched anywhere in the body
#   read LGPL-2.1 as GPL+LGPL, from LGPL's section 3 naming the ordinary GPL; (2) junit-3.8.1 read
#   as GPL+MPL+Python when it is IPL-1.0, a family the predicate did not know; (3) hard wrapping
#   at ~70 columns split "GNU General Public\nLicense" so a flat phrase search MISSED it; (4) a
#   Markdown heading "# Apache License" and a Markdown link "[GNU General Public License ...](...)"
#   both defeated line-anchored and phrase patterns. None of the four was a legal question.
